Q: Apache: How can i see my localhost on 192.168.1.101 from 192.168.1.102? A:

Because the connection is timed out (not refused) I guess it is a firewall problem check if you are using any.

There can still be an other possibility if your kernel is using black holes for closed ports (it does not send connection refused TCP packets just refuses to answer anything if the port is not used). But you mentioned that you have Listen 80 in your config file, and that means all interfaces, so the chances are good you have a firewall problem after all.

In UFW (the default firewall in Ubuntu) you can add a firewall rule to allow incoming HTTP connections to your box:

sudo ufw allow proto tcp from any to 192.168.1.101 port 80

Q: Data Studio regression – visualising data using Chart / Filled Map for Morocco A:

Bro there is no public timeline for a "restoration" because Google treats this as intentional behavior aligned with its policies (not a bug). If it feels like a recent regression in the tool itself, you can:

  • Report it directly in Looker Studio (via the Help menu → Send feedback) with screenshots, your location/account details, and affected report links. Google support sometimes addresses visualization-specific quirks faster than broad mapping policy.

  • Check the official Looker Studio/Google Data Studio community forums or issue trackers for similar reports.

Policies on disputed territories rarely revert quickly due to legal and international considerations.

Workarounds (Temporary or Permanent)

Here are practical options to include the full Moroccan territory (including the Sahara region) in your Filled Maps:

  1. Use a Broader or Custom Geo Scope:

    • Set the map's Zoom Area (in chart setup) to a region like Africa or a custom viewport focused on Morocco. This sometimes affects how sub-regions render.

    • Try dimension values like "Morocco" (full name) or ISO code "MA". Test if including data points explicitly tagged for southern provinces helps.

  2. Switch to Google Maps Chart (instead of plain Filled Map):

    • Looker Studio has a Google Maps chart type (with Filled Area option). It may handle local Moroccan views better since your account/company is Morocco-based.

  3. Custom Data / Blended Approach:

    • Aggregate your data at the country level ("Morocco") instead of splitting regions.

    • Use a calculated field or CASE statement in your data source to normalize all relevant areas under "Morocco".

    • For more precision, blend with a custom lookup table of regions.

  4. Advanced Custom Maps (Stronger Workaround):

    • Looker Studio/Looker supports custom map layers via TopoJSON/GeoJSON files. You can upload or reference a boundary file that depicts Morocco with its full southern territory as a single region. This bypasses Google's default geo resolution.

    • Tools like GeoJSON.io or public sources (with care for accuracy) can help create this. Then configure your chart to use the custom layer.

  5. Account/Location Tweaks (for Testing):

    • Confirm your report/viewer settings, Google account locale, and any VPN/proxy (though being physically in Morocco should favor the integrated view).

    • Share the report with "Anyone with the link" and test viewing from different locations/accounts to observe differences.

  6. Alternative Tools (if needed):

    • Export data and use Tableau, Power BI, or other BI tools with custom shapefiles for full control over boundaries.

    • For static needs, consider image-based visuals or embedded custom maps.

If the issue started only in the past few days, it could also tie into a broader rollout or caching change—try clearing cache, duplicating the report, or recreating the chart from scratch.

Recommendation: Start by reporting the issue via Looker Studio feedback with specifics (chart type, dimension used, expected vs. actual). For immediate needs, the custom TopoJSON approach or aggregating under "Morocco" should get you the desired display.
